Quality and design aids

The optional checks and records that sit beside the main loop: measuring a goal against a baseline, telling the agent how carefully to touch each file, keeping an architecture document and a project memory, and the reviews for risky changes.

On this page
  • Which one when
  • Quality metrics
  • Change zones
  • Architecture document
  • Knowledge graph
  • System graph fragments
  • Whole-repo audit
  • Reviews for risky changes
  • Companion plugins

Most people only need

  • Nothing here is required. The loop runs without any of it.
  • The three reviews for risky changes run when the normal review notices a matching change; you can also run them by hand.
  • Start with /sigma-audit if you want one look at the health of a whole repository.

Each aid below is separate and opt-in unless it says otherwise. None of them changes how the loop picks or merges until you turn it on, and each says what it adds in time or spend.

Which one when

You want to knowUseDefault
Did this goal make a number I care about better or worse?Quality metricsoff
How carefully should the agent touch these files?Change zonesoff
What is the system made of, in one place?Architecture documentoff
What did we learn that the next run should remember?Knowledge graphoff
Which services, endpoints and owners connect, with evidence?System graph fragmentsformat only
Has the whole tree drifted from its own rules?Whole-repo auditon request
Does this change touch auth, a public contract or a migration?Reviews for risky changeson a match, or by hand
Do I want an extra review pass from another plugin?Companion pluginsdetected, never required

Quality metrics

What it is. For each metric command you write, it says whether the goal's head is better, the same or worse than its merge-base, and by how much. It runs only commands you wrote, and when it cannot measure it says unmeasured rather than guess.

Gesture. From inside the goal's worktree, after the work is committed:

python3 <installed-sigma>/skills/sigma-loop/scripts/quality_delta.py <goal>

Config. A quality.metrics list in .sdlc/config.json, absent by default, so nothing runs. Each entry has a name, a command (an argument list, no shell), a direction of lower or higher, and a scope of repo or changed-files. The command prints a number as its last non-empty line and exits 0. The list is read as committed at the merge-base, so a goal cannot loosen the bar it is judged by; commit the config for it to apply.

The merge gate. gates.quality_ratchet.enabled is false by default. When on, a merge measures first: a required metric that is worse beyond its tolerance is measured once more and, if still worse, parks the goal; a required metric that cannot be measured also parks it.

Cost. Two runs of every metric per goal, one at each commit, one at a time, each in a scratch worktree, bounded by timeout_seconds (default 300). No command runs if available memory is under 15 percent of total (a judgement, not a measurement). The gate adds up to quality.gate_timeout_seconds to the merge call. It runs on POSIX only. Metric commands run with credential-shaped environment variables removed, but the list is a denylist, so treat a metric command like your verify command.

Change zones

What it is. A declaration of how carefully to touch a file: leave legacy code almost alone, and design modern code freely. Nothing infers zones; you declare them.

Gesture. The plan phase prints each file's zone and rule. By hand: python3 <installed-sigma>/skills/sigma-loop/scripts/zones.py classify <path>.

Config. design.zones, a list of {"glob": "...", "zone": "legacy" | "modern"}, absent by default. The last matching entry wins, so put the broad one first. A new file always follows sound design; a legacy file is changed only as far as the goal needs. If the zone or the fork point cannot be resolved, it applies no zone rule.

Cost. None to speak of: it reads the config and git, with no network or model call.

Architecture document

What it is. One architecture document per system with a fixed skeleton of eleven sections, a system-context diagram and a container diagram, and a table naming the technology of every container. A linter with no dependencies checks the structure, not the content.

Gesture. /sigma-init --architecture-doc writes the skeleton and prints the commands to add it, which you run. To check it: python3 <installed-sigma>/skills/sigma-init/scripts/architecture_doc.py lint <dir>, which exits 0 clean, 1 with findings, 2 on a usage error.

Config. architecture.system_root, default docs/architecture: a folder inside the repository, or a repository URL (shape-checked only, never fetched). The loop never scaffolds it for you.

Cost. None: no network, no model call.

Knowledge graph

What it is. A project memory that accumulates what Sigma learns, so research compounds instead of evaporating. Web searches are captured as short scrubbed summaries, never the raw page; analysis notes and retrospective lessons are written to .sdlc/knowledge/, which is gitignored so captures stay local. The graph is built by an external tool (graphify by default); if it is not installed, /sigma-kg says so and nothing else changes.

Gesture. /sigma-kg to build, refresh or query. /sigma-context reads it back as a cited brief at the start of a goal.

Config. knowledge_graph.enabled is false by default; scope is full (code and notes) or research (notes only); auto_refresh is false; web_retention_enabled is false.

Cost. Building needs a language-model backend for the builder, and Sigma never picks one, because that would bill you silently. The first build extracts the whole corpus; later refreshes re-bill only what changed. With auto_refresh on, a refresh runs at the end of each retrospective without being asked.

System graph fragments

What it is. A contract for one JSON file saying what a repository's services, endpoints, topics and owners are and how they connect, where every edge carries evidence: its source, a file and line or a URL, a commit, and a confidence. A model-sourced edge is never treated as proof.

Gesture. A read-only check of a fragment, with no network: python3 <installed-sigma>/skills/sigma-kg/scripts/sysgraph.py validate <file>. The page that defines the format says it does not build, merge or query a graph; later work is meant to.

Config. No key. Cost. None: no network or model call.

Whole-repo audit

What it is. A read-only audit of the artifact rather than a single diff: does the tree still obey its own stated rules, what has decayed by accumulation, what debt is measurable, and does the repository still serve its objective. Per-diff review cannot see a smell that took forty small changes to form.

Gesture. /sigma-audit. It reports and files nothing; /sigma-audit --file files at most 8 issues, deduplicated against the open backlog. The report goes to .sdlc/knowledge/audit/ and has at most 12 findings, and it says how many it dropped.

Config. No key. Cost. A script ranks files by size and recent change with no model call; the model then reads only the ranked files, and the report states that read set.

Reviews for risky changes

Three reviews that sit beside the normal code review. When the review phase runs a read-only detector (a shell script, no model call) and it matches a category, it also runs the matching review. You can run any of them by hand. None has a config key of its own.

Security review

/sigma-security-review threat-models a change to authentication, user data, billing, external input or a public endpoint. It lists the entry points, traces the data flow, runs a ten-point checklist (identity, permission, input validation, injection, secrets, cost, dependencies, failure modes, configuration and more) and assigns each finding a severity from critical to info with a remediation. Cost: one extra review pass.

Contract check

/sigma-contract-check looks for breaking changes to a public API, an event shape, a command-line interface, an exported type or an environment variable, by reading every consumer rather than the diff alone. If you declare contracts as frozen, it checks those. Cost: one extra review pass.

Migration check

/sigma-migration-check takes a schema or data migration and produces a plan covering the forward path, the backfill, rollback and a canary read-write. Cost: one extra review pass.

If the project's north-star cannot be located, each of these says that the non-negotiables were not checked, rather than passing silently.

Companion plugins

What it is. Sigma has no plugin dependencies; every phase runs on its own skills. One optional companion, the code-review plugin from Anthropic's official marketplace, adds an extra pass over the diff in the review phase. It never replaces Sigma's own review.

Gesture. None: /sigma-doctor reports it as present or absent, and absent is never an error. Config. companions is "auto" by default; set it to "off" to skip the probe. Cost. The extra review pass is model time.
